data.gender_notes: Rohtas is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A name of Lord Shiva, derived from the Sanskrit word 'Rohtas', which means 'a mountain fort'. The name Rohtas carries the meaning “Mountain Fort” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Rohtas usually hope their child will grow to embody mountain fort and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Rohtas represents the inner strength and courage, and the ability to protect and defend oneself and one's loved ones. It is also a reminder of the protective and powerful presence of Lord Shiva.
data.etymology: Rohtas belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mountain Fort.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rohtas total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The Rohtas name has deep rooted cultural significance in the Indian sub-continent, particularly in the states of Bihar and Jharkhand. It is believed that Lord Shiva, the Hindu god of destruction, once resided in this region and was thus known as Rohtas. The name is reflective of the rich Hindu mythology and history of the land.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Rohtas holds immense spiritual significance for Hindus as it is associated with Lord Shiva, the supreme god of Hinduism who represented destructive and creative powers of the universe. It signifies protection, strength, and devotion, much like a mountain fortress that shields and guards its people. By carrying this name, individuals connect spiritually with the divine power of Shiva and seek his blessings for strength, courage, and wisdom.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Rohtas: Radiant as the Sun in the realm of Dharma. Light of truth and justice, guiding the path towards righteousness.

historical_references.reference: Rohtas was the name of a powerful Vakataka king who ruled from around 505 CE to 512 CE. During his reign, he expanded the Vakataka empire and is known for his grand architectural works, including the rock-cut temples at Bhaja and Karla.

Rohtas is also the name of an ancient city located in present-day Bihar, India, which is believed to have been founded around the 7th century CE. It was a major trading center and fortress city, and is known for its strategic location at the confluence of the Ghaghara and Gandak rivers.
